paragraphs.text: Codebook: Mobility as Social Service
Findings architecture for the lit-review pipeline paper. Built 2026-09-20.
How to read this codebook

Nine findings domains (A to I) plus a method block (M). Domains A to G are transcript and workshop findings; domain H (the discourse the AV carries) and domain I (the charity model and digital food system) are the two new lit-derived domains added from the four literature threads.
Every code carries provenance: T = transcript (SECS AI interviews, focus groups, weaver), W = workshop (Workshop 1 / Capstone ideation, Workshop 3), L = lit-derived. A code with a mix lists the mix.

A single excerpt can carry multiple codes. BREAKDOWN (a live moment of resistance or reframing) folds into domain F as a flag. CAPABILITIES dissolves into A5 and informs C7. CONSTRAINTS are named inside the D codes that own them. No em dash in any field. No fabrication: every quote and citation traces to a source file. Spanish-language quotes are translations, marked translated.
Domain A. Community mobility and care as existing infrastructure

The community already runs its own mobility and care networks: trip-chaining, proxy pickup, redistribution to homebound neighbors, local knowledge. Evidence the paper's claim that community concerns already govern mobility here.
Paper map: C1, C4 | Findings: The community already runs mobility
MODES. Modes of access  (T)
Definition: The concrete ways pantry users physically reach services: car, walk, cycle, family or friend lift, transit, ride-share.
Include: A named travel mode plus a reason for the choice.
Exclude: Hypothetical future modes belong to F (Provocation).
Example quote: "At first, I came on foot and then I started coming in a small car... after a year I managed to buy a small car."  (sec-participant-15-sp, 15:25:38; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (3.1 Modes of access); MaSS: PRACTICES, CONSTRAINTS; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
TRIPCHAIN. Trip-chaining and multi-purpose routing  (T)
Definition: Mobility by folding the pantry into trips already being made: the school run, the Boys and Girls Club, a clinic, work.
Include: A pantry visit described as one leg of an existing journey, or a route chosen because it sits on another purpose.
Exclude: Single-purpose pantry trips; purely digital ordering legs.
Example quote: "I go, pick up my children from school, and at the same time, I pick up my food."  (sec-participant-11-sp, 15:13:20; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (3.1); MaSS: PRACTICES; Capstone: C18c (time constraints)
Thesis clause: C4
CARENET. Care distribution networks  (T)
Definition: Client-run proxy pickup and redistribution: delivering to homebound neighbors, multi-household pickup, redistribution circuits, multi-pantry assembly.
Include: Any description of moving food on behalf of others or assembling a supply from several sources.
Exclude: Formal pantry volunteer programs (Capstone C08); a single household's own logistics.
Example quote: "I have a neighbor that I usually take a box to she's 85 and a cancer survivor. They can't really drive no more."  (focus-group-old-bethel, 01:10:04)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 2 (2.3 reciprocity), Theme 3 (invisible infrastructure); MaSS: CAPABILITIES; Capstone: C17, C18a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 6 context
Thesis clause: C4
LOCALKNOW. Local knowledge and informal information networks  (T)
Definition: Neighborhood knowledge that routes food and care: who is homebound, which stores overcharge, which pantry has meat, benefit changes.
Include: Information shared person to person about where, when, or how to access resources.
Exclude: Institutional outreach or marketing (Capstone C03 second tier belongs to F).
Example quote: "They quick with the word of mouth. And that's the original internet right there."  (focus-group-old-bethel, 01:13:45)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 1 (discovery), Theme 4 (4.8 information delay); MaSS: CAPABILITIES; Capstone: C03 (second tier, awareness)
Thesis clause: C4
CAPABILITIES. Capabilities and assets  (T)
Definition: Existing community resources and informal systems already accomplishing mobility and care: multilingualism, self-taught skill, credentials, trip-chaining, persistence.
Include: Existing assets or systems, not wished-for ones.
Exclude: Requests or wishes for capabilities that do not yet exist.
Example quote: "we've been in this neighborhood all our life."  (focus-group-hope, 00:50:12)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 5 (needs), Theme 7 (aspirations); MaSS: CAPABILITIES; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
MEANINGS. Meanings of mobility  (T)
Definition: What mobility represents: caregiving, being seen, dignity, independence, progress, human contact.
Include: Evaluative statements about what a trip, a vehicle, or a delivery signifies.
Exclude: Functional descriptions of how trips happen (A2, A3).
Example quote: "striving to be someone better in life."  (sec-participant-15-sp, 15:30:03; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9, Theme 7; MaSS: MEANINGS; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
LOAD. Material burden of the trip  (T)
Definition: The physical and environmental cost of moving food home: carrying capacity, the return-with-goods leg, weather exposure, bulk versus the bus.
Include: A named difficulty carrying groceries, walking home loaded, or braving weather.
Exclude: The dollar cost of a trip (D10).
Example quote: "the most challenging part is going back because I have the bags."  (ministries-of-love-interview-walker, 01:46, Speaker 2)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (3.3 Physical and logistical friction); MaSS: CONSTRAINTS; Capstone: C16 (last mile), C08 (carrying heavy loads)
Thesis clause: C4
Domain B. Values that govern mobility here
The values at stake in this context: equitable access, relational trust, flexibility for variable need, plus dignity, stability, self-reliance, family and faith anchors, and choice as respect.
Paper map: C4 | Findings: The values at stake
JUST_ACCESS. Equitable access  (T)
Definition: The value that people can get to services when they need them, regardless of rigid slots, geography, documents, language, or cost.
Include: Statements framing access-when-needed as what matters, or naming a barrier to it.
Exclude: Generic "everyone should have a ride" with no access barrier named.
Example quote: "Homebound people miss out on transportation ideations."  (workshop-3-codesign, cluster: Home Bound)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3, Theme 5; MaSS: JUST_ACCESS; Capstone: C17, C18
Lit evidence: Equity thread, clause 4 (97.4% direct or partial)
Thesis clause: C4
JUST_TRUST. Relational trust, being known  (T)
Definition: The value of trust placed in known persons and being recognized, not trust in a system or vehicle.
Include: Trust in staff, comfort from being known, confidence that someone will listen.
Exclude: Trust framed as trust in technology reliability (goes to H3, EFF_VALUE).

Example quote: "here with them, they give you confidence, they listen to you... anything, they let me know through a message or text message or WhatsApp message."  (sec-participant-15-sp, 15:27:26; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (staff kindness), Theme 4 (4.7 trust building); MaSS: JUST_TRUST; Capstone: F11 IDEA_TRUST (privacy and trust family)
Lit evidence: Mechanism 2, read as contrast
Thesis clause: C4
JUST_FLEX. Flexibility for variable need  (T)
Definition: The value that the service adapts to fluctuating, unpredictable need: household size, timing, one-off vs recurring.
Include: Statements valuing adaptability, spontaneity, or being served when the opportunity arises.
Exclude: Fixed scheduling described neutrally with no flexibility concern.
Example quote: "Whenever I have the opportunity, whenever I have the opportunity, chances to go."  (sec-participant-13-sp, 15:14:56; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4, Theme 5 (5.4 flexible scheduling); MaSS: JUST_FLEXIBILITY; Capstone: C18c
Thesis clause: C4
DIGNITY. Dignity, non-judgment, being seen  (T)
Definition: The value of being treated without shame or surveillance, and being seen as a person, not a case.
Include: Statements about shame, stigma, comfort, non-discrimination, being looked down on.
Exclude: Stigma as a system-side barrier belongs to D or E; here it is the value being asserted.
Example quote: "To be looked down upon."  (sec-participant-06, 15:52:46)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4 (4.10 fear of judgment), Theme 9; MaSS: VALUES; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 7 (dignity literature)
Thesis clause: C4
STABILITY. Stability, not abundance  (T)
Definition: The aspiration is steadiness and predictability, not more: sufficiency, income predictability, a quiet place.
Include: Statements naming steadiness, predictability, or modest sufficiency as the goal.
Exclude: Growth-oriented aspirations coded under A6.
Example quote: "they just want stability. They want to be able to. Have what they need, have it, and then be able to get what they want."  (ministries-of-love-interview-walker, 03:18, Speaker 2)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 7 (7.1 foundation of stability); MaSS: VALUES; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
SELFRELY. Self-reliance and autonomy  (T)
Definition: The value placed on independence and being able to take care of oneself, which can both motivate and delay asking for help.
Include: Statements naming self-reliance as a virtue or as a barrier to receiving help.
Exclude: Design recommendations about user control (C3).
Example quote: "I want freedom from being broke."  (focus-group-hope, 00:14:09, Speaker 1)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 2 (2.4 autonomy); MaSS: VALUES; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
ANCHORS. Family, faith, and community as anchors  (T)
Definition: The named sources of endurance: family and children, faith, community belonging, personal will.
Include: Anything that keeps someone going, named as the motivation to persist.
Exclude: Motivations for pantry use specifically (OG Theme 2).
Example quote: "Family." then "Willingness to help."  (sec-participant-14, 15:24:06 and 15:24:20)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 8 (motivations); MaSS: VALUES; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
CHOICE. Choice and personalization as respect  (T)
Definition: The value that being able to select items and paths is itself a form of respect and dignity.
Include: Statements that choosing mattered, or that inability to choose felt like disrespect.
Exclude: Food selection as a pure logistics detail.
Example quote: "You could choose your own items... So we didn't get stuff we didn't need and not use it."  (sec-participant-02, turns 3 and 4)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (cannot choose items), Theme 6; MaSS: VALUES, JUST_FLEXIBILITY; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
Domain C. Alignment: what works

Design features that already work in this context and why: human connection, being known, choice, dual contact paths, operational ease, efficiency that serves. Includes one lit-derived positive finding (community-built alternatives).
Paper map: C4, C7 | Findings: What already works
STICKY. Human connection as the sticky factor  (T)
Definition: What keeps clients returning is the personal, non-discriminatory treatment, not the food supply.
Include: Praise of staff kindness, sincerity, welcome; loyalty explained by relationship.
Exclude: Praise for operational ease (C5) or for choice (C3).
Example quote: "they feel comfortable with Old Bethel because they know it's a church pantry... more compassionate, more understanding, more empathetic."  (focus-group-old-bethel, 01:20:40)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (9.1 staff kindness); MaSS: JUST_TRUST, VALUES; Capstone: C16 (human touch at delivery)
Lit evidence: Mechanism 7
Thesis clause: C4
EXCEPTIONS. Being known earns exceptions  (T)
Definition: Staff who recognize a client personally grant flexibility that written policy forbids.
Include: Instances where personal recognition produced a rule exception.
Exclude: Policy-level flexibility; hypothetical flexibility.

Example quote: "she knows I come. So when she has to go to work on those Saturdays, she allows me to pick it up for her and my dad. And some people are like, nope, they got to be here."  (focus-group-hope, 00:51:15, Speaker 8)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9; MaSS: JUST_TRUST; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
CHOICEWORKS. Choice as a working design feature  (T)
Definition: Where choice exists it works: SEC's selection model and clothing program are praised on both dignity and waste grounds.
Include: Evidence that user selection reduced waste, met dietary need, or felt respectful.
Exclude: The no-choice box model (D2, D3).
Example quote: "they have a lot of food options."  (sec-participant-22, 16:40:18)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9; MaSS: JUST_FLEXIBILITY, JUST_ACCESS; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
DUALPATH. Low- and high-contact paths, user-chosen  (T)
Definition: Both a low-contact path (drive-through) and a high-contact path (personal greeting) serve different clients; the ideal is client choice.
Include: Preferences for either path, or evidence each path serves someone specific.
Exclude: Adoption-metric logic (G3).
Example quote: "Having the sense of not being around a lot of people and being able to just drive through."  (sec-participant-05, 15:55:08)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (operational ease); MaSS: JUST_FLEXIBILITY; Capstone: C16 (human touch at delivery)
Lit evidence: Mechanism 6 (workshop case work)
Thesis clause: C4
OPEASE. Operational ease and reliability  (T)
Definition: Praise for how easy and reliable the operation is: simple ordering, food ready on arrival, drive-through pickup.
Include: Positive statements about the mechanics of pickup or ordering.
Exclude: Efficiency that constrains or excludes (D domain, F8).
Example quote: "I'm usually coming here right after work."  (sec-participant-16, 15:53:46)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (operational ease); MaSS: PRACTICES; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C4
EFF_SERVES. Efficiency that serves  (T)
Definition: The paper should not treat efficiency and community value as always opposed: appointment slots serve the fixed-shift worker, the drive-through serves the anxious client.
Include: An efficiency feature working for a specific client type, with the client named.
Exclude: Efficiency adopted for its own sake (D1, F8).
Example quote: "That I don't have to miss work."  (sec-participant-16, 15:54:21)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9; MaSS: JUST_ACCESS; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
COMMUNITY_BUILT. Community-built alternatives outperform agency defaults  (L)

Definition: When residents or community organizations are resourced to build their own plan, scenario, or design rather than only react to one, the result can match or outperform the agency or industry default on the sponsor's own terms.
Include: Any lit claim that a community-authored alternative matched or beat a default, or evidence the community already runs what the formal system forbids.
Exclude: Consultation that collects input without influence (E7).
Example quote: [LIT] No transcript exemplar yet; see Lit evidence map.
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a (new); MaSS: CAPABILITIES close; Capstone: n/a

Lit evidence: Mechanism 6: Karner et al. 2020; Gripper et al. 2022; Severs et al. 2022; Prost et al. 2018; Heitlinger et al. 2021; Baumann et al. 2018; Sörries et al. 2024; Gomes et al. 2026; Pineo et al. 2026
Thesis clause: C7
Domain D. Misalignment: system logic vs. community value

The system side does X for efficiency or legibility and it costs value Y. Each code names the operative logic (efficiency, rationing, verification, scheduling, digitization, language, eligibility, cost externalization).
Paper map: C3, C5 | Findings: Where system logic costs community value
EFF_VALUE. Efficiency framing: throughput, optimization, automation-as-improvement  (T)
Definition: The system side invokes efficiency logic: speed, optimized routing, throughput, scheduling precision, automation-as-improvement.
Include: A named efficiency or optimization logic on the provider side, including the design team's own instinct.
Exclude: Vehicle or tech mention with no efficiency framing.

Example quote: "How might we use AVs to reduce logistic company cost (labor, time, asset) to improve the distribution efficiency and have workforce capacity to fulfill other social services needs"  (workshop-1-codesign, CLUSTER: Workforce Optimization (effect), HMW)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 9 (rigid policies implicit); MaSS: EFF_VALUE; Capstone: C05, C08, C09, C10
Lit evidence: Mechanism 3: Park, Jang, and Ko 2024; Lu et al. 2020; Pimenta et al. 2023; Zhang et al. 2019
Thesis clause: C3
RATIONING. Rationing and standardization  (T)
Definition: The system side caps frequency, runs lotteries, or pre-packs uniform boxes; the client loses the ability to plan and loses selection.
Include: Caps, lotteries, apps that run out, standard boxes, experienced as unfair, unplannable, or unhealthy.
Exclude: A neutral description of a scheduling system with no burden named.
Example quote: "What, once a week? No, once a month."  (sec-participant-22, 16:39:27)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4, Theme 9 (supply gaps); MaSS: MISALIGNMENT; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
VERIFY. Verification and legibility regimes  (T)
Definition: The system side requires the beneficiary to appear in person with ID, or substitutes machine verification for recognition, to keep the count legible and prevent fraud.
Include: ID and self-collection requirements, face verification, the "show your ID, move on" line, and what the rule criminalizes.
Exclude: Permission to use a proxy or delivery is the positive counter (C2, G2).
Example quote: "everybody's got a card, their number, show their ID, move on."  (focus-group-old-bethel, 14:46)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (pantry policy), Theme 9 (rigid policies); MaSS: MISALIGNMENT; Capstone: C04 (face verification)
Lit evidence: Mechanism 5 (surveillance side)
Thesis clause: C5
FIXEDSCHED. Fixed scheduling and appointment slots  (T)
Definition: The system side runs fixed distribution windows and appointment slots, which serve the predictable-schedule user and fail the variable-hours user.
Include: Named schedules, Saturday-morning windows, appointment-only models, and who they exclude or serve.
Exclude: Scheduling praised as serving a specific client (C5, EFF_SERVES).
Example quote: "Food pantry works on Saturday mornings - many families work at that time."  (workshop-3-codesign, cluster: Time)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4, Theme 5 (5.4 flexible scheduling); MaSS: JUST_FLEXIBILITY close; Capstone: C12 (expanding hours as contrast)
Thesis clause: C5
DIGITONLY. Digital-only access  (T)
Definition: Moving resource navigation, job applications, and pantry ordering online assumes a device, a data plan, and literacy.
Include: Named digital assumptions: no paper application, "not everybody has the phone", online ordering that hides services.
Exclude: SEC's online ordering praised by the digitally fluent (C5).
Example quote: "not everybody has the phone."  (focus-group-ministries-of-love, 00:45:16, Speaker 3)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4 (pathway uncertainty); MaSS: MISALIGNMENT; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 3: Joassart-Marcelli et al. 2026; Deener 2017
Thesis clause: C5
LANGTRANS. Language as transaction, not trust  (T)
Definition: The system side provides a translator at the counter; what Spanish-speaking clients want is a relationship in their language, which an interpreter does not build.
Include: Requests for Spanish-speaking staff, for classes, or statements that a translator alone does not create trust.
Exclude: Language as a desired service outcome (OG Theme 5.2).

Example quote: "They always have a translator, but it would be good to have someone who can assist us in Spanish a bit and teach us to speak a bit of English."  (sec-participant-04-sp, 16:14:37; translated)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 5 (5.2 language and cultural integration); MaSS: JUST_TRUST; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
INVISIBLE. Wraparound invisibility: services are unknown and un-navigable  (T)

Definition: Job coaching, financial guidance, and education services exist alongside food, but most clients do not know they exist, and when told cannot find a usable path in; referrals go unanswered.
Include: Not knowing services exist, website not describing them, a referral that never generates follow-up.
Exclude: Awareness of food services only.
Example quote: "It's not really described on the website very well. I would say that I'm not at the right, you know, location on the website."  (sec-participant-21, 16:39:01)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4 (4.1 to 4.9); MaSS: MISALIGNMENT; Capstone: C03 (awareness)
Thesis clause: C5
ELIGGATE. Eligibility gates: zip code, benefit thresholds, documents  (T)
Definition: Defining a service area and verifying eligibility gates people out of better-stocked pantries by where they live and what they can produce.
Include: Zip-code exclusions, income or document gates, turning people away at intake.
Exclude: Benefit cliffs are coded as D9.
Example quote: "You can't go under the zip code."  (focus-group-hope, 00:43:39)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (pantry policy); MaSS: MISALIGNMENT; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
CLIFFS. Benefit cliffs and policy traps  (T)
Definition: Benefits cut off at thresholds: $74 over earns nothing, food-stamp ineligibility, childcare vouchers on hold, hours cut while costs stay.
Include: A named threshold or policy rule that eliminated a benefit or trapped a household.
Exclude: General mention of low income with no threshold named.
Example quote: "my dad was $74 over. $74 over, so you don't get nothing."  (focus-group-hope, 00:41:07)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 6 (9.10 policy barriers); MaSS: CONSTRAINTS close; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
COSTOUT. Cost externalization: the trip is on the client  (T)
Definition: The pantry addresses food, not the cost of reaching it: gas, a car payment, $25 to $30 for a ride against a $2 bus that does not stop nearby.
Include: Any named trip cost the service leaves to the client, including fuel poverty.
Exclude: Carrying or weather burden (A7).
Example quote: "not having gas all the time."  (sec-participant-12, 15:05:44)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 3 (3.2 financial mobility barriers); MaSS: CONSTRAINTS; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C5
Domain E. Participation gap: infrastructure without community

How decisions land on people who had no say. Extends the three MaSS input codes with lit-derived codes on consultation without power, performative vs authentic equity, and negative political self-efficacy.
Paper map: C2, C6 | Findings: Infrastructure without the community
INPUT_ABSENT. No say: plans land without the community  (T)
Definition: The community currently has no say in how mobility and services are decided: decisions land on people who had no seat at the table.
Include: Statements that needs are not accommodated, that routes, sites, or services are decided elsewhere.
Exclude: Lacking a ride rather than lacking a say (code as D10 or A).
Example quote: "Neighbor have ideas imposed on them. Their needs are not accommodated"  (workshop-3-codesign, cluster: People centered, Input/decision making)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4; MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 1, 4: Pinski et al. 2024; Hicks et al. 2025; van Holstein et al. 2020
Thesis clause: C2
INPUT_PRESENT. Rare participation that did shape a decision  (W)
Definition: A moment where participation did shape a decision, including this co-design workshop being named as a rare instance.
Include: Evidence that community or stakeholder input changed an outcome.
Exclude: Hypothetical "it would be nice to be asked" codes as INPUT_ABSENT.
Example quote: [No verbatim quote; this co-design session is itself the instance. Coders log workshop ID and speaker role.]
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a; MaSS: INPUT_PART_PRESENT; Capstone: The Capstone ideation itself
Lit evidence: Mechanism 1, 6
Thesis clause: C2
PURPOSE. Purpose exclusion: who decided this was the goal  (T)
Definition: Questions not just how the AV or service is built but why it exists and who decided the goal; the design point is pulled by sponsor interest and adoption rather than need.
Include: Challenges to the goal itself, including ROI and adoption framing on the design side.
Exclude: Questions about design details only (routing, hours).
Example quote: "Biggest ROI of AV as a social service is the adoption rate of AV"  (workshop-3-codesign, SECTION: How would AV works in terms of service?, cluster: Current Infrastructure)
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a; MaSS: PURPOSE_EXCLUSION; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 3: Van Wynsberghe and Guimaraes Pereira 2022; McCullough et al. 2024
Thesis clause: C6
IMPOSITION. Imposition and displacement  (T)
Definition: Things get put in the neighborhood regardless of protest: a shelter, a data center, a route.
Include: Named decisions imposed on a community, whether they happened or were resisted.
Exclude: Renaming and erasure (E5).
Example quote: "the people that got the money, they're going to do it anyhow. It don't matter if you protest or not."  (focus-group-hope, 00:45:02, Speaker 7)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4; MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 4
Thesis clause: C2
ERASURE. Symbolic exclusion: renaming and erasing  (T)
Definition: Institutions rename themselves away from community and service, and data rules erase the capacities staff relied on.
Include: Renaming that removed "community" or "service" from a name; a data-collection rule that erased interpreter planning.
Exclude: Neutral rebranding with no stated loss.
Example quote: "you took the community out"  (focus-group-hope, 00:57:03)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 4; MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT; Capstone: n/a
Thesis clause: C2
STAGED_EFF. Participation staged but efficiency-run  (W)
Definition: Even in a room asked to design for the community, the first design instinct is efficiency: driver reduction, 24/7 operation, face verification, waste extraction.
Include: Logistics and optimization ideas produced in the co-design sessions.
Exclude: The people-and-place family of the same sessions codes to F9, F10, F12.
Example quote: "AV can anticipate the shortage of food. No communication from human"  (workshop-1-codesign, CLUSTER: Communication (features), Idea)
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a; MaSS: EFF_VALUE close; Capstone: C05, C07, C10
Lit evidence: Mechanism 5 (friction lens)
Thesis clause: C2
CONSULT_NO_POWER. Consultation without binding influence  (L)
Definition: Formal public involvement processes solicit community input through meetings, committees, or task forces, but rarely give that input binding influence over the final decision.
Include: Lit evidence that an inclusive-sounding process reproduced exclusion or collected input without power transfer.
Exclude: Community-built alternatives with real authority (C7).
Example quote: [LIT] No transcript exemplar yet; see Lit evidence map.
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a (new); MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT close; Capstone: n/a

Lit evidence: Mechanism 1: Pinski et al. 2024; Bailey et al. 2012; Karner et al. 2020; McCullough et al. 2024; van Holstein et al. 2020; Klaever et al. 2025; Hicks, Kingsley, and Isett 2025; Barendregt, Bendor, and van Eekelen 2024; Cresswell Riol and Connelly 2025; Joassart-Marcelli, Bosco, and McFadden 2026
Thesis clause: C2
PERF_VS_AUTH. Performative vs authentic equity  (L)
Definition: Equity practices that claim inclusion without redistributing decision-making power (performative) versus those that do (authentic).
Include: Lit claims distinguishing performative inclusion from real power transfer.
Exclude: Simple consultation logistics.
Example quote: [LIT] No transcript exemplar yet; see Lit evidence map.
Source cross-refs: OG: n/a (new); MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT close; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 1: McCullough et al. 2024
Thesis clause: C2
NEGATIVE_SELFEFF. Negative political self-efficacy  (L)
Definition: People stop participating entirely after being ignored or humiliated: prior negative experiences teach them their input will not be needed.
Include: A client's expressed doubt that speaking up matters, plus the lit mechanism.
Exclude: General service distrust without a participation referent.
Example quote: "I don't know if somebody's going to actually listen or whatever"  (sec-participant-01, turn 21, Interviewee)
Source cross-refs: OG: OG Theme 10.1 (legitimacy and trust); MaSS: INPUT_PART_ABSENT close; Capstone: n/a
Lit evidence: Mechanism 2: Klaever et al. 2025
Thesis clause: C6
Domain F. Provocation: what happens when we ask about AVs
What the speculative AV prompt surfaced, by respondent group: community, stakeholders, and the design team (Workshop 1 / Capstone ideation). Design-team ideas sit here as contrast.
Paper map: C6 | Findings / method: What the AV prompt surfaced
SPEC_UPTAKE. Speculative uptake  (T)
